correctness.rationale: For all finite connected simple unweighted graphs with combinatorial L=D-A and edge variation ∑edges|f(u)-f(v)|, the coarea indicator decomposition gives the exact operator norm as a maximum over nontrivial cut indicators. Differentiating each crossing edge and same-side edge of e^{-tL}1_S gives K(S)=-∑c_S(v)^2+∑_{internal uv}|c_S(u)-c_S(v)|. Finite maxima give the right derivative max K/|∂S|. If nonpositive, operator-norm submultiplicativity of the semigroup and b(t/N)^N≤(1+o(1/N))^N show all-time contraction; positive K gives a constructive counterexample. Bridge side cut has K=deg(u)+deg(v)-4. Together with the long-cycle three-vertex cut and pentagon three-leaf obstruction, necessity leaves precisely bare cycles; triangle/square with ≤one leaf per cycle vertex; pentagon with ≤two distinct leaves. Recomputed exact 40 allowed graph configurations, all 3,064 nontrivial cut slopes, and compared direct directional derivatives; all satisfy K≤0 and match (-6, -4, -2, 0) table. Long-cycle witnesses k=6,7,9 gave K=1. Original script inspected, not accepted merely because of log marker. The seven-vertex signal separates edge-TV from Lipschitz contraction.
